authorization: Publisher authorised three verified daily company-analysis articles on 2 November 2026, superseding the repository's one-new-article daily cap.
story_thesis: Audience and bookings growth are producing higher Mobility and Delivery profit, but autonomy spending, stock compensation, debt and investment activity determine whether scale improves value per share.

identity.units: USD millions except users, trips and per-share data

duplicate_checks: Checked EDITORIAL_TOPIC_INDEX.md, CONTENT_INVENTORY.md, data/content-inventory.json and actual wealth Markdown; Uber had a maintained stock profile but no dedicated audience-growth and operating-leverage analysis.
Checked open PRs 57 and 43, recent merged publication PRs, company-publication records and live content; no matching Uber story or fingerprint was active.
Checked the 5 November Europe/Dublin scheduled publication count before drafting; no scheduled company-analysis article had been published.
The article tests durable platform economics; routine quarterly figures remain on /stocks/uber/.
candidate_review: Uber: selected for bookings growth, segment leverage and autonomy/platform spending.
McDonald's: selected separately for guest counts and franchise economics.
CVS Health: selected separately for separation and segment economics.
AppLovin: screened but not selected because advertising-platform coverage risked overlapping recent monetisation analysis.
Qualcomm: screened but not selected because AI-device and data-centre questions overlapped existing AI infrastructure coverage.
Datadog: screened but not selected because a cleaner non-overlapping cash-conversion question was not established.
Allstate: screened but not selected to rotate away from another insurance-led article alongside CVS.
Arista Networks, AMD and Super Micro Computer: screened but not selected because the canonical AI-infrastructure earnings article already addresses the core question.

evidence_table.claim: MAPCs were 215m, trips 4.061bn and gross bookings USD59.819bn, up 14%, 16% and 20%.
evidence_table.location_or_arithmetic: Release KPI and segment tables; periods and reported growth rechecked.

evidence_table.claim: Mobility segment income was USD2.362bn on USD29.512bn bookings; Delivery USD1.057bn on USD28.539bn.
evidence_table.result: verified; calculated margins labelled as Compound calculations

evidence_table.claim: Revenue grew 10%, with business-model changes reducing growth by eight percentage points.
evidence_table.location_or_arithmetic: Release revenue table and explanation; gross bookings are not described as revenue.

evidence_table.claim: R&D expense was USD1.273bn, up 48%; management targets about 700 driverless vehicles at year end and more than 2,000 during 2027.
evidence_table.location_or_arithmetic: 10-Q operating-expense table and release management commentary; vehicle numbers labelled targets and R&D not wholly attributed to autonomy.

evidence_table.claim: Q3 OCF was USD2.639bn, capex USD104m and company-defined FCF USD2.535bn; nine-month SBC was USD1.614bn and repurchases USD4.279bn.
evidence_table.result: verified; GAAP and non-GAAP measures separated

evidence_table.claim: Long-term debt rose to USD15.664bn from USD10.521bn while cash and short-term investments were about USD10.1bn.
evidence_table.location_or_arithmetic: 10-Q balance sheet and financing cash-flow lines; borrowing, repayment and investment activity rechecked.

fact_check_pass.method: Every material number, period, segment label, accounting measure, management target and calculation was reread against the SEC-furnished release and Form 10-Q; arithmetic was recomputed independently.
